extracted.intended_audience: Wesleyan undergraduates and prospective English majors
extracted.subtask_description: Learning outcomes and program goals for Wesleyan's English undergraduate program, covering literary study, critical writing, and creative writing practice. Targets students enrolled in or considering the English major.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical thinking about literature, culture, and history
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of literature fosters critical thinking about the relationships among literature, culture and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students develop the ability to think critically about how literature interacts with cultural and historical contexts; this is presented as a central aim of the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adept criticism of literary genres and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Students become adept critics of poetry, novels, essays, and plays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly names poetry, novels, essays, and plays as forms students should learn to critique; implies close reading skills across genres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of the history of literary culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop knowledge of the history of literary culture and about the evolving genres, forms, and ideologies of literary expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes familiarity with historical development and change in genres, forms, and ideological contexts as part of the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding literary texts in historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the relation of literary texts to their historical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative expectation is that students situate texts historically and analyze how context shapes meaning and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reading of political speech and popular culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to read critically in political speech, popular culture, and the discourses that structure everyday life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends literary-critical skills beyond canonical texts to contemporary and nonliterary discourses, signaling applied critical literacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hone skills as critical writers
rubrics_metrics.description: As they develop their knowledge, students of English hone their skills as critical writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied curricular outcome: students are trained to produce well-argued, critically engaged scholarship and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop creative-voice and produce new literary texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore their potential as creative voices; faculty and students work together to ... create new literary texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program supports creative writing alongside critical study, emphasizing mentorship and collaborative production of new work.
